sections.heading: Best Starter & Mid-Game Value Choices
sections.intro: Your first weapons set the pace for museum progression. Pistols and shotguns form the natural entry point—both are affordable, immediately available in the shop, and deal reliable damage across the museum's opening wings.
paragraphs: Pistols offer the lowest barrier to entry and teach core aiming mechanics. They cost minimal cash to purchase and upgrade, making them ideal for players still learning destruction physics and object breakage patterns. While individual pistol shots deal modest damage, their rapid fire and low recoil let you practice precision on high-value targets like chandeliers and statues, which pay out significantly more than generic museum décor. Use your first 2–3 runs with pistols to map the museum layout, identify lucrative breakable zones, and build a cash reserve without overthinking loadout complexity.

Shotguns represent the next progression step and deliver a substantial damage spike for their cost. They excel at close-range destruction of clustered objects—perfect for museum rooms packed with vases, glass displays, and wall-mounted art. The upfront purchase price is slightly higher than pistols, but the destruction efficiency gain justifies the investment around run three to five, once you've accumulated enough cash. Shotguns also synergize well with the museum's physics engine: tight groupings of destructible objects break faster when hit simultaneously, accelerating your cash-earning pace.

The mid-game pivot arrives when your cash reserves reach 500–1000 in-game currency (exact thresholds vary by your destruction efficiency and wing progression). At this point, you face a strategic choice: continue upgrading pistols and shotguns for marginal returns, or redirect funds toward unlocking a specialized mid-tier weapon. Sledgehammers and laser cutters emerge as strong options here. Sledgehammers provide raw area-of-effect damage, flattening entire object clusters with a single swing and reducing the time per room. Laser cutters unlock methodical destruction of tougher materials and hidden object types, opening new cash sources you couldn't access with basic firearms.

Timing your mid-game weapon purchase matters as much as which weapon you choose. Avoid the common mistake of splitting purchases—buying a little of this, upgrading a little of that. Instead, commit your reserve to one mid-tier weapon once you've identified which museum wing comes next in your progression. Check the museum map or wing unlock requirements beforehand, then invest in the weapon best suited to that environment. This focused approach accelerates your transition into late-game tiers and sets up synergies with secret weapons you'll discover.

Every wing hides a secret weapon, and discovering these can dramatically shift your mid-game strategy. While full secret locations are covered in the dedicated Secrets guide, the tactical lesson here is simple: before spending heavily on a new mid-tier purchase, invest 10–15 minutes exploring your current wing for hidden tools. Finding even one free secret weapon can delay or entirely skip a mid-tier purchase, freeing cash for the late-game nuke or singularity unlock.

Cash efficiency compounds over multiple runs. A well-sequenced early-to-mid progression (pistol → shotgun → mid-tier specialist) typically reaches late-game weapon eligibility 2–3 runs faster than random or simultaneous purchases. Use the leaderboard as a loose benchmark: players ranking high in glass broken and time spent are usually executing this progression discipline correctly. Your mid-game goal is not to optimize every penny, but to establish a predictable earning rhythm that funds late-game dominance without unnecessary grinding.
